clue.text: The Dodo Drier — with prizes for all

definitions.text: The Dodo Drier — with prizes for all

parts.words: The Dodo Drier — with prizes for all
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Dodo organises a running game to dry off the soaked animals, and declares that everybody has won and all must have prizes

explanation.surface: An odd advertisement for a drying machine named after an extinct bird, with everyone a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the event in Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland: the creatures run round in a circle until dry, and the Dodo rules that all have won.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's chapter title names this aimless race, now also an idiom for a contest where everyone gets a reward.

clue.text: The priest who may not be better without it ?

definitions.text: who may not be better without it
definitions.meaning: a remedy, without which a patient may not recover

explanation.surface: A clergyman whose presence might make you well again.
explanation.definitionFit: A French parish priest, and a remedy that makes the sick well.

clue.text: A son needs this inner prompting to operate

indicators.note: the word for son must have this put inside it, so the answer is what is left when son is taken out

parts.note: a surgeon is one whose job is to operate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy has to feel an inner drive to get things working.
explanation.walkthrough: S-ON with the answer inside makes the one who operates; take SON out of SURGEON to leave the letters wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong impulse or desire is a prompting to act.

clue.text: Like a mule — began an awkward spell

definitions.text: Like a mule — began an awkward spell

indicators.note: spell the letters in an awkward way, that is, rearrange them

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A stubborn animal starts one of its difficult moods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward spell' rearranges A MULE BEGAN AN; the whole clue also describes a mule, hard to control.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is proverbially stubborn, so it cannot be handled or controlled.

clue.text: The mountains are in shooting distance

definitions.meaning: the distance a gun can reach

explanation.surface: The hills are close enough to fire at.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of hills, and the reach of a gun or missile.

clue.text: Charles is taken in by Edward and is beaten

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the short name for Edward

parts.note: Ted is a pet name for Edward
taken as written

explanation.surface: Charles is fooled by Edward and loses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests fooled, but it puts IS inside TED. 'and is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be punished physically or scolded is to be beaten in the old sense of corrected.

clue.text: There's a way round Company Tax

indicators.note: the street abbreviation is placed so that it goes round the company abbreviation

parts.note: ST, short for street, a kind of way

explanation.surface: Someone has found a way to dodge corporation tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' is only a link. Scot is an old word for a tax or levy, surviving in 'scot-free'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old levy or payment, the sense kept in the phrase meaning untaxed or unpunished.

clue.text: What's cooking ? Something 25 perhaps

definitions.meaning: a mixture of ingredients being prepared
25 refers to the clue Made up: an invented story

explanation.surface: Asking what is on the stove, maybe something imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewed mixture of ingredients, and an invented tale or lie.

clue.text: Not Silver Blaze-though Holmes was able to

definitions.text: Not Silver Blaze-though Holmes was able to

parts.words: Not Silver Blaze-though Holmes was able to
parts.note: in the Sherlock Holmes story Silver Blaze is a missing racehorse that Holmes manages to track down; a draught animal in harness is not a racer

explanation.walkthrough: Silver Blaze is a racehorse, not a draught animal that pulls by the traces; yet Holmes did find it, or trace the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra horse harnessed by traces to help pull a load uphill is unlike a racer, yet Holmes tracked one down.

clue.text: This reunion one might term genial

indicators.note: the clue says the words term genial might be something else, which here means rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Old soldiers' get-together that one could only describe as friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one might' is the anagram signal: TERM GENIAL, rearranged, gives the adjective one would apply to a gathering of old soldiers. The definition is loose, describing the kind of reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion of former members of an army unit is described by this adjective for things belonging to that unit.

clue.text: A happy whistler, anyway

indicators.note: read any way, forwards or backwards, the name stays the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful who whistles, at any rate.
explanation.walkthrough: In the musical The King and I the governess sings 'I Whistle a Happy Tune'. 'anyway' read as 'any way' says the name is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of The King and I sings that she whistles a cheerful tune whenever she feels afraid.

clue.text: A capital line for a bishop

definitions.meaning: the London Underground line named after the capital
an archbishop with authority over a province

explanation.surface: A London Tube route that takes a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A London Underground line, and a senior bishop over a church province.

clue.text: Taking a shower, confidentially, in the garden

definitions.meaning: standing beneath the perforated sprinkler head of a shower or watering can, which is called a rose
the Latin sub rosa, meaning in secret
beneath a rosebush among the flower beds

explanation.surface: Someone tells you privately that they are washing outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in secret (Latin sub rosa), and literally beneath a sprinkler head or a garden bloom.

clue.text: " quiet as a nun, with adoration" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: quiet as a nun, with adoration" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: quiet as a nun, with adoration" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: the missing word from Wordsworth's sonnet It is a beauteous evening, describing a nun hushed in worship

explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's sonnet describes the holy evening as hushed like a nun, scarcely drawing air in adoration.

clue.text: Where's Reynard hiding — or at least his hind legs ?

definitions.text: Where's Reynard hiding — or at least his hind legs

parts.words: Where's Reynard hiding — or at least his hind legs
parts.note: Reynard is the fox; he hides in thick shrubs, and his tail is called his brush, so his hind legs are beneath it

explanation.walkthrough: A fox's tail is its brush, so the legs at the back lie beneath the brush.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense shrubs and saplings in a wood give a fox cover, and the phrase also places the legs beneath the tail.

clue.text: Vagabonds smuggle semi-precious stones

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running
agates are banded semi-precious stones

explanation.surface: Wandering criminals sneak gemstones across the border.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for runaways or wanderers, a synonym of tramps.

clue.text: The endless plunder causes palpitation

indicators.note: the last letter of the word the is cut off

parts.note: plunder means robbing as a noun

explanation.surface: Being robbed without end makes the heart race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the E from THE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid pulsing of the heart is a beating or pounding.

clue.text: A relationship that was the end of Nelson

indicators.note: only the end of the name is kept, the first two letters being dropped

parts.note: Admiral Nelson's first name was Horatio

explanation.surface: A love affair that finished off the famous admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Nelson's affair with Emma Hamilton; in fact only the end of his first name, Horatio, is wanted, losing its first two letters HO.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a proportion between two quantities is a relation between them.

clue.text: Lone wolf

parts.note: in Kipling's Jungle Book the leader of the Seeonee wolf pack is called the great grey Lone Wolf

explanation.definitionFit: Kipling names the pack leader in The Jungle Book this, and Cub Scout leaders take the title from him.

clue.text: Counsel lifemanship tactics when one reorganizes the labour force

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for counsel or advice
lifemanship is the art of getting one over on others, and its tactics are ploys

explanation.surface: Legal advisers use one-upmanship tricks when a manager reshuffles the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a barrister but is the archaic noun REDE. 'when one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy workers afresh is to move them to new jobs or places.

clue.text: The noise of the water-pipe

definitions.meaning: a bubbling, gurgling sound, or idle chatter
a hookah, whose smoke is drawn through water

explanation.surface: The gurgling that a hookah makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming term names both a bubbling sound and the hookah that makes it.

clue.text: An unruly tribe can be dangerous

definitions.text: An unruly tribe can be dangerous

indicators.note: the letters of tribe are unruly, out of order, and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawless clan may be a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges TRIBE; the whole clue describes something that can bite and is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: One that bites, like a savage dog, can do harm.

clue.text: In charge of raising mathematical points

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are lifted up, so read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In charge of lifting mathematical points.
explanation.definitionFit: Points where rays meet or which define a curve, plural of focus.

clue.text: "The is full of noises" (Tempest)

parts.note: Caliban's speech in The Tempest begins Be not afeard, describing Prospero's island

explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play Caliban says the island where they live is full of sounds and sweet airs.

clue.text: A case: of imprisonment in The Tuileries

indicators.note: the answer is held captive inside the words The Tuileries

explanation.surface: A trial about someone locked up in the Paris palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the French royal family held in the Tuileries; 'imprisonment in' signals the letters held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental needle-case is called by this French word.

clue.text: Made up

parts.note: invented, not true, as a story is

explanation.definitionFit: An invented story is not real, so it is imaginary or false.

clue.text: A quarter squared in London

parts.note: a district of central London that has a square bearing its name

explanation.definitionFit: This West End district of London has a well-known square named after it.

clue.text: Make a mountain out of a molehill when reading gas, perhaps ?

definitions.text: Make a mountain out of a molehill

indicators.note: these words might perhaps become something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Exaggerate wildly when checking the gas meter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reading gas' looks like checking a meter, or the gas works at Reading; 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange READING GAS. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate is to inflate something's importance, as overstating a small matter does.
